# One child process per run-scope, reaped when the scope closes

Sibling run-scopes in one frame do not share a late-bound executor process. The
daemon spawns one child per run-scope and reaps it when that scope closes.

## The template

A fan-out with three partitions and parallelism three, dispatching a late-bound
service:

```yaml
name: run-scope-demo
version: "1"
late_bind_services: [devsvc]
nodes:
  - type: worker
    executor: devsvc
    claim_producers:
      - name: claim-producer-filesystem
        selector: data
        intent: rw
        alias: parent
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    fan_out:
      claim: parent
      partition_request: '{"list":[{"key":"p1"},{"key":"p2"},{"key":"p3"}]}'
      parallelism: 3
      error_policy:
        kind: strict
```

Bind it to a binary that holds each execution open, so all three siblings are in
flight at once:

```json
"service_bindings": {
  "devsvc": {"path": "/path/to/binary", "env": {"SERVICE_HOLD_SECONDS": "20"}}
}
```

## While the siblings are in flight

```bash
rimsky daemon status --state-dir ~/.rimsky/daemon
```

The daemon lists three spawned children, each naming a different run-scope, each
with its own spawn id, all from the one declared binding path. Three separate
operating-system processes are running the bound binary.

The three executions report three different run-scopes and three different
process ids, in a one-to-one pairing. Every child reports its own in-memory
counter at one, so no process served a second run-scope's call and no run-scope
saw another's in-process state.

The daemon spawned three children in total — one per run-scope, not one per
dispatch and not one shared.

## After the fan-out settles

```bash
rimsky daemon status --state-dir ~/.rimsky/daemon
# spawned children: none
```

The child list empties and no process is left running the bound binary, while
the daemon itself stays connected. Children are reaped when their run-scopes
close, not when the daemon stops, so a long-lived daemon driving many fan-outs
does not accumulate processes.
